item.title: Sacred Heart Academy claims SCC volleyball title over Amity behind JJ Kirck's 31 digs
item.description: The Sacred Heart Academy girls volleyball team celebrates its SCC title after beating Amity 3-2 on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, at West Haven High School. (Mike Madera/For Hearst Connecticut Media) WEST HAVEN - It is often said that offense wins games and defense wins championships. Sacred Heart Academy senior libero JJ Kirck will attest to that. Playing spectacular defense, including 31 digs, Kirck was one of the keys in leading the second-seeded Sharks to a 3-2 (21-25, 25-11, 25-19, 23-25, 15-11) victory over top-seeded Amity in the Southern Connecticut Conference championship game at West Haven High on Thursday evening. "Our team battled all year," Kirck said after being named the tournament's Most Outstanding Player. "We played so many different games this year, and every game besides one, we came out on top. Tonight was just a show of how much we faced adversity." The Sharks avenged consecutive SCC championship game losses to Amity and improved to 20-1 on the season. "It means everything to me," Kirck said. "I'm from Amity. I love all these girls across the net. I grew up playing volleyball with all of them. I am so glad my senior year, I was able to get the dub, and I am so glad I was able to do it with my best friends." Both teams entered the contest without losing a set thus far in the SCC tournament. Amity, which has been in the final every year since 2021 and won two in a row over the Sharks, delivered the first blow in handing Sacred Heart Academy its first set loss of the tournament by riding the play of Calleigh Parkin and Brooke Cichon in the opening set. The Sharks pushed back and dominated the second set with a 14-point win that saw a kill by Aliya Church put the Sharks ahead 16-8 and her ace extend the lead to 20-9. "Their defense played really well," Amity coach Seth Davis said after his team fell to 19-3 on the year. "They dig a lot of balls. They pass really well. Once we started passing, we could keep the ball in system and get the ball to Olive (Hubbard)." The two teams used strong defensive play to split the next two sets as Kirck's defense thwarted Amity in the third set before she closed it out with a pair of service points. The Spartans would not go quietly, overcoming a 21-19 fourth-set deficit with a pair of kills by SCC Player of the Year Olive Hubbard, a kill by Parkin, and a block by Hubbard to close the set. "We did our job from the service line," Sacred Heart Academy coach Dave Alexandro said. "Tough serves to the seams, and it kind of took them out of system which allowed us to get some swings on the ball, and then build up a little bit of a lead. With that confidence, swinging well, hitting the ball well, kind of moving them around the court made a big difference." The turning point came in the fifth set when a block by Paige Nelson gave Sacred Heart Academy a 10-9 lead. item.title: Elder's Kaden Estep is rewriting Panther records in senior season
item.description: Nearly 40 years ago, Steve Keller dominated the Elder Panther quarterback records. The starting quarterback in 1987 and 1988, Keller amassed 4,816 yards and 45 touchdowns in his career. Twenty years after Keller, Mark Miller led Elder to the Division I state championship game in 2008 and the semifinals in 2009. Along the way, he broke both of Keller's career records with 5,872 yards and 56 touchdowns. Miller's touchdown record still stands, but his yardage record didn't get that 20-year cushion. First, Peyton Ramsey broke it with 6,708 yards (and took second with 49 touchdowns) from 2013 to 2015, but the Elder record books were rewritten again in 2026 and the pencil is still sharpened to take down another. Elder senior quarterback and Cincinnati Bearcats commit Kaden Estep broke Ramsey's record with a 13-yard pass to Jake Bier in a 62-6 win over Mount Zion Prep on Oct. 23. Estep finished the game with 6,861 career passing yards. His five touchdown passes in that game put him at 53 for his career, just three behind Miller. "Earned," Ramsey, now an assistant coach at Elder, posted on X after Estep's record-breaking night . "The greatest QB to ever put on the uniform. Period. An absolute winner. All of it a byproduct of the type of teammate he is. Keep going!" Since Estep took over as a sophomore in 2024, Elder has gone 26-9, including an undefeated 2025 regular season and Greater Catholic-League South championship . It was Elder's first GCL-South crown since Ramsey led Elder to a split with St. Xavier in 2015 and first solo title since Miller led the Panthers in '08. Seeing Ramsey initially break his yardage record was a full-circle moment. item.title: Why Grizzlies’ Isaiah Stewart has ‘no regrets’ on wild LeBron James altercation
item.description: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Why Grizzlies’ Isaiah Stewart has ‘no regrets’ on wild LeBron James altercation appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Isaiah Stewart has built a reputation as one of the NBA’s most fiery players, and the Memphis Grizzlies big man is not about to apologize for it. Looking back on his infamous altercation with LeBron James and other run-ins, Stewart made it clear he does not regret a thing. In an interview with Andscape, Stewart was asked whether he had any regrets about those incidents or if it was simply the emotion of the moment. “I don’t have no regrets. You know, I feel like there’s lessons out of everything. You know, even going back to that first incident, you know, Charlotte, like I don’t have no regrets and I don’t care what people may perceive me as,” Stewart said. “I come to play basketball and I play the game a certain way. And it has been times where, you know, I thought back and say, hey, I shouldn’t have done that.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Isaiah Stewart says he has no regrets about trying to fight LeBron James 😳 (Via @andscape / h/t @0xBassey ) pic.twitter.com/WrXxsGevz9 — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 5, 2026 Stewart also called out opponents he believes try to bait him into losing his cool. “And I feel like teams having their game plan of, hey, let’s do something to trip him off, to get him out the game. For me, it’s hard to respect you as a man if that’s your game plan,” he said. The LeBron incident remains the most memorable of Stewart’s career. Back in November 2021, James struck Stewart in the face with an elbow while the two were battling for position during a free throw, leaving the then-Detroit Pistons big man bloodied. An enraged Stewart repeatedly charged after James and had to be held back. James was ejected and later suspended one game, while Stewart received a two-game suspension. His most recent suspension came in February 2026, when Stewart left the bench to join a fight between the Pistons and the Charlotte Hornets . The NBA handed him a seven-game ban, citing his “repeated history of unsportsmanlike acts.” It was his fourth suspension for fighting. A few months later, Detroit traded Stewart to the Grizzlies for three future second-round picks during the 2026 NBA Draf t, ending his six-season run with the Pistons. Now 25 years old, Stewart is part of a Grizzlies team that is off to a 6-2 start. Based on his comments, he has no plans of changing the way he plays anytime soon. item.title: Unfair NIL: Millionaire Quarterbacks, Broke Linemen
item.description: Oct 31, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Auburn Tigers offensive lineman Jacobe' Ward (74) blocks during the third quarter against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The numbers are finally in, and they tell a story that leaves many fans scratching their heads. A new database released on Friday by the College Sports Commission reveals just how wide the gap is between star quarterbacks and the players in the trenches. According to Fox Sports , the market is bearing a heavy load for some while others fly blind. John Bramlette, the head of operations for the commission, admitted that “Everyone to some degree or another has probably been flying blind as far as what the market is actually bearing.” This lack of clarity has left schools and athletes guessing for far too long. The Millionaire Quarterback vs. The Working Class Lineman Let’s be honest about the disparity. The data shows that the top 10 percent of paid Power Four quarterbacks are receiving $1.611 million in revenue share alone, with combined NIL and revenue-share totals climbing higher at the extreme end. That official College Sports Commission figure lines up with earlier summer estimates from Opendorse and others that already put elite quarterbacks well into seven figures. Meanwhile, the median pay for players in other spots, like the offensive line or defensive back, is a fraction of that. It is a system where the face of the program gets the big checks , but the guys blocking for him are often just scraping by. This is about football and who gets valued in the eyes of the market. The report sorted the money by position and conference, giving us a clear look at the divide. The revenue sharing for the top tier hit $662,000, making the gap between Power Four and non-Power Four schools in men’s basketball dramatic regarding high-end spending. Football follows a similar pattern, but the stakes for the players at the bottom are much higher. The data might not capture every single dollar, but it reflects the reality that many players have tried to report on in less official ways.

item.title: Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? Making sense of trade rumors around star RB
item.description: Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? Making sense of trade rumors around star RB originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Ravens , once 4-1 and near the top of the AFC, are in serious trouble after four consecutive losses. Not only is Baltimore last in the AFC North at 4-5, but the Ravens might not have Lamar Jackson back on the field this season after thumb surgery. Help is on the way, as veteran Jacoby Brissett is coming over from the Cardinals in a trade to take over at quarterback, but it might take a heroic effort for Baltimore to turn its season around. With the trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, would the Ravens consider trading future Hall of Fame RB Derrick Henry? Here's what you need to know about the rumors surrounding Henry. MORE: Can Ravens still make the playoffs? Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? The future of Henry is something to "keep half an eye on," ESPN's Dan Graziano reported before the Ravens' loss to the Jaguars . "Henry is turning 33 in January. He is scheduled to earn $12 million next year, and none of that money is guaranteed," Graziano said. "If he isn't in Baltimore's plans beyond this year, the Ravens could find themselves fielding offers over the next week." Fielding offers isn't the same as shopping a player, but as the math becomes more difficult for the Ravens in the AFC, Graziano lists a handful of reasons why a trade could make sense, from Henry's age and contract to the reality of trying to win without Jackson. The number of contenders in need of a running back could also get the Ravens some value in a trade. Several teams, including the Giants , Broncos , Bengals , Vikings and Packers , have been reported as suitors for Indianapolis' Jonathan Taylor. Only one of them can get him. Could the losers of that sweepstakes make a play for Henry? Teams being interested in Henry is no surprise. The Ravens willingly talking about deals involving Henry is a separate subject, and to this point, no reports have indicated they are looking to deal their running back. With Brissett coming in and a more favorable portion of the schedule ahead, one would think Baltimore still has visions of competing this season. If the Ravens wanted to get something for Henry, though, the best time might be right now. Already down to their third-string quarterback, the Ravens have now lost safety Kyle Hamilton for the rest of their Thursday Night Football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, Hamilton will not return after suffering a hip injury . He had already been dealing with a knee injury that kept him out of practice the previous week . He also has one interception and a forced fumble. Hamilton’s injury adds to the Ravens’ already lengthy injury list in the secondary. Cornerback Nate Wiggins was listed as inactive shortly before the Jags game due to illness . Safety Jaylinn Hawkins was also listed as out. It remains to be seen whether this latest injury will keep Hamilton out for their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers. But they will have a lengthy 11-day break before that game, which should give him time to recover. But if it is in any way serious, the Ravens are unlikely to risk sending him out amid his other injury concerns. With the Ravens’ season increasingly looking lost amid their quarterback injuries, they will be wise to exercise caution moving forward. item.title: ‘He’s special’: Ayo Dosunmu says Timberwolves have a ‘trash talker’ who’s just like Muhammad Ali
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Ayo Dosunmu has heaped praise on Anthony Edwards and has compared the Minnesota Timberwolves star to Muhammad Ali and three NBA greats. The 26-year-old joined the Wolves in February this year, and he has built a great relationship with all of his new teammates in Minnesota. Edwards, in particular, has become a good pal, and Dosunmu has given an insight into what the Ant-Man is actually like. Ayo Dosunmu compares Anthony Edwards to Muhammad Ali Edwards is arguably the biggest star on the Minnesota Timberwolves roster. The 25-year-old had an unbelievable start to the season, but is currently sidelined following surgery on his knee. The initial diagnosis was that he would be out for around two months. The Timberwolves have missed Edwards, but everyone associated with the team is convinced that he will come back stronger. That is because of his mentality, which every member of the Wolves roster has constantly seen – not just during games but in practice as well. Dosunmu said about Edwards in The Players’ Tribune : “Ant. He’s special. As a trash talker, he’s like what you hear about with the Kobe (Bryant) stories, the MJ (Michael Jordan) stories, the KG (Kevin Garnett) stories. No, really, I think a better comparison is like the (Muhammad) Ali stories. “He’s jogging back after a bucket like: ‘Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee! I’m a bad man! I’m so pretty!!!'” Edwards isn’t just a really talented player, but his personality is incredible as well. That is why he is so loved, not just by the fans but by his teammates as well. The Minnesota Timberwolves need their star man back. If he hits the ground running once he returns, there is every chance they will achieve their ambitions this season. item.title: Gabriel Vs. Magomedov: 4 Keys To Victory In ONE Lightweight MMA Main Event At ONE Fight Night 49
item.description: Two unbeaten runs collide in the main event of ONE Fight Night 49 on Prime Video , and only one will make it out intact. Lucas Gabriel puts his unblemished promotional record on the line against undefeated newcomer Magomed “Muhammad” Magomedov in a highly pivotal lightweight MMA showdown. The three-round war, carrying massive potential World Title implications, goes down live in U.S. primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, November 6. View this post on Instagram Gabriel has seamlessly carved through six appearances in ONE Championship without suffering a single defeat. The 26-year-old earned the most significant victory of his career this past June, outpointing former divisional king Ok Rae Yoon at ONE Fight Night 44 . With ONE Lightweight MMA World Champion Christian “The Warrior” Lee defending his crown against ONE Welterweight Submission Grappling World Champion Tye Ruotolo at The Inner Circle 37 , a statement win could instantly make Gabriel the undisputed next man in line. Magomedov, meanwhile, carries a flawless 15-0 professional record into his promotional debut. The KHK Dagestan standout fearlessly stepped in on short notice for the injured Alibeg Rasulov , making the leap to the global stage riding five consecutive finishes. With a high-level black belt’s craft set directly against suffocating Dagestani-style pressure, here are the four tactical keys that will ultimately decide which unbeaten run lives on. #1 Gabriel’s Scramble-Ready Guard Photo Credit: ONE Championship Putting a Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt on his back can create more problems than it solves. item.title: Three takeaways from Michigan State's win over Toledo
item.description: Michigan State basketball improved to 2-0 on the season Thursday night when the Spartans defeated the Toledo Rockets, 91-61. It was another convincing win from MSU, who are showing the strength of this team early in the year. In the win, Michigan State had four in double figures, while the team shot 50.9% from the field to go along with a stellar 41.7% three-point percentage. The team outrebounded the Rockets 52-27, but lost the turnover battle 14-11. In the end, the Spartans got a convincing win over the Rockets, and continued to show that the hype that came into the season was warranted. Take a look at the three takeaways Spartans Wire had from the win over Toledo: 1. Another convincing win It may be a 37-point win over Quinnipiac and a 30-point win over Toledo, but the Spartans taking care of inferior competition and doing it in convincing fashion should not go unnoticed. Too many teams of the past, or other top ranked teams find themselves letting lesser teams hang around, but the Spartans taking care of their business shows a lot about this team. Being able to come in and dominate games like this shows that this team is ready to be a big time player across the landscape of college basketball this season. 2. Jasiah Jervis In the win against Toledo, it was Jasiah Jervis's coming out party. The true freshman finished with 16-points on 5-of-9 shooting, while going 4-for-7 from three. After a underwhelming debut against the Bobcats, it was great to see Jervis excel against Toledo. If the Spartans are going to hit their ceiling this season, Jervis is going to have to be a major component in the Spartans success. 3. Free throw shooting After two good things, there has to come a bad, and that is the Spartans free throw shooting. After a 15-for-26 night against Quinnipiac from the line, the Spartans followed it up with a 23-for-38 performance agaisnt the Rockets. There is no secret here, this is pitiful and Tom Izzo knows it. The Spartans are going to need to drastically improve their performance at the line if the team plans to have success in the tough road ahead. item.description: Westlake head coach Rick Clausen directs his players during a practice on Aug. 11, 2026, at Westlake High. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Rick Clausen is not backing down from the parents who hired private investigators to dig into his Westlake High School program. He told reporters that some kids and families feel entitled to certain things. He said that mindset belongs to the old Westlake and does not align with the program’s direction going forward. Clausen added that everything in his program is earned through competition. He declared he would not apologize for constructing a program based on good families and good kids with college goals. item.description: Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars threw for 242 yards and a touchdown pass (Patrick Smith) Trevor Lawrence guided the Jacksonville Jaguars to a straightforward 33-10 victory Thursday over a desperate Baltimore Ravens team forced to rely on its ailing third-string quarterback. item.title: Jones - the smiling wind-up artist who refuses to fade away
item.description: Eddie Jones has coached in Australia, England, Japan and South Africa [Getty Images] An Eddie Jones press conference has always been an event in itself. You never quite know what's coming. A compliment, a cutting observation, a verbal grenade. Sometimes all three, invariably delivered with that mischievous smile. Jones belongs to a disappearing generation of coaches who understood that the contest could begin long before the players took the field. Warren Gatland could intimidate with his imposing presence and gruff demeanour alone. Jose Mourinho proclaimed himself 'The Special One' and made confrontation an art form. Jones was different. Small in stature, with an almost permanent grin, he could stir up an entire nation while thoroughly enjoying himself. All three built reputations on dominance. Not simply on the pitch, but over the agenda, their players and the organisations they represented. But the language of coaching is changing. Wales head coach Steve Tandy talks about connection and relationships. Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler emphasises collaboration, trust and understanding the person behind the player. Neither lacks ambition or authority, but their approach contrasts with the era of the all-powerful head coach. At 66, Jones remains one of rugby's most fascinating characters from that old school. The method behind the mischief In 2018 Jones questioned whether Wales fly-half Rhys Patchell could handle the pressure of playing England at Twickenham, while describing Warren Gatland's team as "confident and cocky". But his provocations sometimes crossed the line. That same year Jones apologised after footage emerged of him using some choice language to describe Wales and Ireland in less than flattering terms at a sponsors' event the previous year. The former was classic Jones. Identify a weakness, plant a seed of doubt and ensure everyone was talking about it. The latter showed when the wind-ups went too far. But how much was calculated? Speaking to BBC Sport prior to Japan's Nations Championship meeting with Wales, Jones offered an intriguing explanation. "Some of them were planned to an extent. Others might have come out of the press conference. Sometimes you say things at the press conference that you don't mean to say. But, yeah, sometimes." "And particularly with England, I always felt with the English that they didn't have enough confidence in themselves." England? Lacking confidence? Jones explained that part of his responsibility was to provide that self-belief. "So I felt one of my roles was to give them that confidence, to be almost the battering ram for them." item.title: Minkah Fitzpatrick Does Damage Control Over Jets Drama
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Minkah Fitzpatrick cleared the air on Thursday, stating he actually said “Jets beating Jets,” not “Jets being Jets,” to explain the team’s self-inflicted errors. The veteran safety i nsists the comment never caused a stir inside the locker room, even as the 2-6 team fights to salvage their season. He believes the team knows exactly what he meant and that the media noise is just a distraction from the real goal: winning games. The New York Post reported that Fitzpatrick spoke on Thursday about the confusion following Sunday’s loss to the Raiders. He emphasized that the context of his words was clear to everyone in the room. “It hasn’t really caused any stir within this locker room,” Fitzpatrick said. “That’s the most important thing. Everyone in this locker room knew what I was talking about.” This focus on internal unity is crucial for a squad that has lost six of its last seven games. Distraction or Reality Check The controversy bothered Fitzpatrick more than anyone else because it threatened to take focus away from the field. He noted that talking about words he might have misused does not help a team trying to win. “It more so bothered me in the moment, when we’re a team that’s fighting to win, and we’re talking about stuff that doesn’t really matter,” he explained. The Jets are now set to face a Kansas City Chiefs team that has dropped two straight games after a hot start. Fitzpatrick is right to push past the noise. The team’s record shows a clear need for better execution, not more drama. He stated, “Our focus and objective now is to win and not focus on should’ve, would’ve, could’ve.” This mindset is the only path forward for a group that hasn’t won since beating the Browns on Oct. 11. The team needs to stop looking back and start looking at the next opponent. Injury Concerns Loom Large While the defense tries to stay focused, the offense faces its own hurdles. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson did not practice again on Thursday while remaining in concussion protocol. His absence would force the offense to rely heavily on other players like Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich admitted that Wilson is unique and hard to replace, yet the team remains confident in their depth. “In one respect, you can’t replace Garrett Wilson,” Reich said. “He’s a unique player. But on the other hand, we’re not afraid.” The team will adjust their game plan based on who is available on Sunday. David Bailey returned to full practice on Thursday after dealing with a groin injury, giving the line some stability. The Jets can only hope that things get better from here, because it can’t get much worse. The road ahead is steep for New York. They enter Sunday’s game in Kansas City looking to snap a losing streak, but that won’t happen unless they fix their penalties and miscues.
